tacat

transaminase catalysis knowledge graph

three PLP-dependent transaminase reactions · an OWL ontology, reasoned at build time, served over SPARQL 1.1

kundai sachikonye · NFDI4Cat demo project

one question

which reactions involve a given molecule as a reactant or product?

the molecule: L-glutamate — CHEBI:29985

two queries

has L-glutamate as a participant
SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?r) AS ?n) WHERE {
  ?r tacat:hasParticipant ?p .
  ?p tacat:participatingEntity ?e .

  ?e a obo:CHEBI_29985 .
}
produces L-glutamate
SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?r) AS ?n) WHERE {
  ?r tacat:hasParticipant ?p .
  ?p tacat:participatingEntity ?e ;
     tacat:participantRole tacat:Product .
  ?e a obo:CHEBI_29985 .
}

two answers

4

reactions have it

3

reactions produce it

the one that drops out is glutamate dehydrogenase

participation is n-ary

an entity, a role and a coefficient — three things at once

modelling reactions

what a reaction model has to account for — and where each one lives here

the concernwhere it lives here
reactants / productsparticipantRole — an SBO term, not a predicate name
stoichiometry factorsstoichiometricCoefficient on the bridge node
class – instance relationthe node's rdf:type is the ChEBI class
conditionsnot carried — would need a process model
stereo chemistrynot carried — the ChEBI microspecies pins it; the model does not reason over it

nothing is asserted

TransaminationReaction is a defined class, declared in Owlready2 — necessary and sufficient, over chemical classes and roles, never over molecules

the artefact the build produces

reuse external terms, mint local instances

the link is rdf:type
tacat:CHEBI_57972
    a  obo:CHEBI_57972 ,        # the external class
       tacat:AminoAcid ;
    rdfs:label  "L-alanine" .

ChEBI, Rhea and UniProt all publish these as classes. Our node is an instance of one — so class membership is the relation that is exactly true, and it needs no predicate of its own.

what the predecessor did
tacat:CHEBI_57972
    ex:chebiIRI
      "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_57972" .

a literal is not a node. A federated join against it returns

zero rows, silently

well-formed · resolvable · unjoinable — and nothing tells you

the identifier is the join key

three reactions here; the proteins are not here — an external service supplies them

recorded

what the definition does not constrain

four conjuncts are a participant-role signature — not a mechanism

not constrainedwhat carrying it would take
that a group actually movedatom mapping — reaction-centre alignment, not participant sets
that the donor is an amino acid at allan omega-/amine transaminase runs amine + keto acid, so two conjuncts fail. Needs alpha- and omega- as siblings under a parent requiring only the transfer
mass and charge balanceSHACL over formulae, or a balance check at build time
additional participantsclosure on the participant set — a closed-world constraint
PLP dependence, the mechanismcarried on the enzyme as a datum; encoding it needs a process model

OWL infers under an open world; SHACL validates under a closed one. Both run.

what you can run

  • reaction type inferred at build time — no reasoner in the request path
  • competency questions are the specification and the regression suite

answered by the Docker image CI built and pushed — not by anything on this laptop

recorded

that is the model. this is the software.

brief steps 3, 4 and 5 — the endpoint, the container, the pipeline

read-only by decision

the app is FastAPI — and the module that decides what may run imports no web framework and names no status code

the rulewhy it is a decision, not an accident
four read forms onlySELECT ASK CONSTRUCT DESCRIBE. Updates fail today because rdflib's parser rejects them — a property of the library, not a choice
SERVICE refused by policya federated clause makes this server fetch a caller-chosen URL and hand back the response. That is SSRF, not a feature — so the rule is a rule, and the guard that implements it is the part worth attacking
a scanner, not a regexSELECT ?service is a legal query. A keyword blacklist refuses it; a whitelist on query form does not
a row cap, not a timeoutrdflib offers no way to interrupt a running query. The README says that, rather than implying hardening

the seam

reasoning happens when the image is built — never when a request is served

both stages start FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim — the same uv base image, so the two stages resolve identically and only the graph crosses between them

builder stage
  • installs a JRE
  • uv sync --frozen, from the lock
  • runs HermiT once
  • writes the reasoned graph

if the reasoner fails, the image does not build — an ontology that cannot be classified is a broken build, not a runtime surprise

runtime stage
  • copies the finished graph
  • serves it under uvicorn
  • no Java at all
  • no network needed

so it answers ?r a tacat:TransaminationReaction — an inferred type — from plain SPARQL, with no reasoner in the request path

the gates check the data

an image can build perfectly while the graph inside it is wrong

stagewhat it proves
qualitylint, types, security — the ordinary ones
verifythree of its four jobs check data, not code: the ontology is consistent and the inference fires; the build is byte-reproducible; SHACL conforms, run with --metashacl so a mistyped shape fails loudly instead of constraining nothing
buildit compiles — Kaniko, so no privileged runner
smokethe pushed image is started as a service and asserted against over HTTP

the inference gate asserts that nothing is asserted, that exactly three are derived, and that the control is not — because a defined class that classifies nothing passes a consistency check in silence

the questions are the tests

the specification is the regression suite — CQ01–04 quoted from NFDI4Cat's own set

11

competency questions

9/9

of the original nine, passed with every identifier wrong

2

CQ10 and CQ11, added because of it

every oracle projected a label — and the label and the identifier are two fields of one row, so corrupting the identifier changed nothing a test could see.
